title: Luke Chapter 24 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 24 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 24 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 24.

questions.question: In Luke 24, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: They found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre
Two men stood by them in shining garments
They came unto the sepulchre bringing spices
Peter ran unto the sepulchre
questions.correctAnswer: They came unto the sepulchre bringing spices
questions.explanation: Luke 24:1 states that they came unto the sepulchre bringing spices very early in the morning, which is the first event described in the chapter.

questions.question: What did they find rolled away from the sepulchre?
options: The stone
The door
The burial cloth
The tomb's entrance
questions.correctAnswer: The stone
questions.explanation: Luke 24:2 says they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.

questions.question: What did they find missing inside the sepulchre?
options: The body of the Lord Jesus
The spices they brought
The linen cloths
The angels
questions.correctAnswer: The body of the Lord Jesus
questions.explanation: Luke 24:3 states they entered and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.

questions.question: Who stood by them in shining garments?
options: Two men
An angel
Jesus
Two women
questions.correctAnswer: Two men
questions.explanation: Luke 24:4 says two men stood by them in shining garments.

questions.question: What question did the men in shining garments ask?
options: Why seek ye the living among the dead?
Have you seen Jesus?
Where is the body?
Why are you afraid?
questions.correctAnswer: Why seek ye the living among the dead?
questions.explanation: Luke 24:5 records that they said, 'Why seek ye the living among the dead?'

questions.question: According to the men in shining garments, where is Jesus?
options: He is not here, but is risen
He is in Galilee
He is with the Father
He is in the tomb
questions.correctAnswer: He is not here, but is risen
questions.explanation: Luke 24:6 states, 'He is not here, but is risen.'

questions.question: What did Jesus say must happen to the Son of Man?
options: Be delivered into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise again on the third day
Be worshiped by all nations
Be crowned king immediately
Be taken to heaven without suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Be delivered into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise again on the third day
questions.explanation: Luke 24:7 states the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise again on the third day.

questions.question: Who told the apostles about the empty tomb and the message?
options: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and other women
Peter and John
Two men in shining garments
The disciples on the road to Emmaus
questions.correctAnswer: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and other women
questions.explanation: Luke 24:10 says it was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and other women who told the apostles.

questions.question: How did the apostles react to the women's words about the resurrection?
options: They thought they were idle tales and did not believe them
They immediately believed them
They were filled with joy
They went to the tomb to see for themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They thought they were idle tales and did not believe them
questions.explanation: Luke 24:11 states their words seemed to the apostles as idle tales and they believed them not.

questions.question: What did Peter find when he ran to the sepulchre?
options: The linen clothes laid by themselves
Jesus' body still there
The stone still in place
The women praying
questions.correctAnswer: The linen clothes laid by themselves
questions.explanation: Luke 24:12 describes Peter stooping down and seeing the linen clothes laid by themselves.

questions.question: To which village did two of the disciples go on the same day as the resurrection?
options: Emmaus
Bethany
Jericho
Nazareth
questions.correctAnswer: Emmaus
questions.explanation: Luke 24:13 states that two of them went to a village called Emmaus.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus himself came near and walked with the two disciples on the road to Emmaus.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 24:15 says Jesus himself drew near and went with them.

questions.question: True or False: The two disciples' eyes were prevented from recognizing Jesus as he walked with them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 24:16 states their eyes were holden so they should not know him.

questions.question: True or False: The two men in shining garments told the women that Jesus was still in the tomb.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 24:6 clearly says Jesus is not here, but is risen, so they did not say He was still in the tomb.

questions.question: True or False: The text says that Peter carried Jesus' body away from the tomb.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 24:12 says Peter saw the linen clothes and departed wondering, but it does not say he carried Jesus' body away.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 24 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 24 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Luke 24:19, how is Jesus of Nazareth described by the two disciples on the road to Emmaus?
options: A prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people
A teacher of the law only
A political rebel against Rome
A wealthy landowner
questions.correctAnswer: A prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people
questions.explanation: Luke 24:19 states that Jesus was 'a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,' describing his powerful ministry.

questions.question: What does Luke 24:26 promise will happen if someone understands that Christ ought to have suffered as explained in Luke 24:25?
options: They will grasp the necessity of Christ's suffering and glory
They will receive immediate wealth
They will be exempt from suffering
They will gain political power
questions.correctAnswer: They will grasp the necessity of Christ's suffering and glory
questions.explanation: Luke 24:25-26 shows Jesus rebuking them for being slow to believe the prophets and then explains that Christ 'ought to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory,' teaching the necessity of suffering before glory.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the disciples when the women told them about the empty tomb and the vision of angels according to Luke 24:22-24?
options: They were astonished but hesitant to believe
They immediately believed and rejoiced
They ignored the women completely
They went to the authorities to report
questions.correctAnswer: They were astonished but hesitant to believe
questions.explanation: Luke 24:22-24 shows the disciples were astonished by the women's report and the vision of angels but still cautious, as some went to the tomb and found it as said but did not see Jesus.

questions.question: How does Luke 24:30-31 connect with Luke 24:28-29 in the story of the disciples on the road to Emmaus?
options: The disciples invite Jesus to stay, and then recognize Him when He breaks bread
Jesus rebukes the disciples for not believing and then disappears suddenly
The disciples leave Jesus and do not recognize Him
Jesus heals the disciples before leaving
questions.correctAnswer: The disciples invite Jesus to stay, and then recognize Him when He breaks bread
questions.explanation: Luke 24:28-29 describes the disciples urging Jesus to stay with them, and Luke 24:30-31 shows that while He was at the table breaking bread, their eyes were opened and they recognized Him.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith can be learned from the disciples being 'slow of heart to believe' as stated in Luke 24:25?
options: Faith requires openness to God's word even when difficult to understand
Faith guarantees immediate understanding
Faith eliminates the need for scripture
Faith is irrelevant to understanding prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires openness to God's word even when difficult to understand
questions.explanation: Luke 24:25 rebukes the disciples for their slowness to believe the prophets; this teaches that faith involves patience and willingness to trust God's revelations.

questions.question: What does the breaking of bread signify in Luke 24:30-31 in the context of recognizing Jesus?
options: It signifies Jesus’ presence and the opening of spiritual eyes
It is just a meal with no special meaning
It symbolizes a farewell
It indicates a ritual cleansing
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies Jesus’ presence and the opening of spiritual eyes
questions.explanation: Luke 24:30-31 shows that when Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, their eyes were opened and they recognized Him, indicating the spiritual significance of the act.

questions.question: How does the experience of the disciples on the road to Emmaus in Luke 24:32 encourage believers in their personal study of Scripture?
options: It encourages believers that Scripture can ignite spiritual understanding and fervor
It suggests Scripture is confusing and should be avoided
It implies only leaders can understand Scripture
It states that Scripture is irrelevant after resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages believers that Scripture can ignite spiritual understanding and fervor
questions.explanation: Luke 24:32 records the disciples saying their hearts burned within them as Jesus opened the Scriptures, showing that Scripture study can inspire and deepen faith.

questions.question: What does Luke 24:34 affirm about Jesus’ resurrection and appearance?
options: The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon
Jesus remains in the tomb
The resurrection was just a story
Only angels appeared, not Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon
questions.explanation: Luke 24:34 confirms that Jesus truly rose and appeared to Simon Peter, affirming the reality of the resurrection.

questions.question: What significance does Luke 24:36 highlight about Jesus' appearance to the disciples?
options: Jesus stands in their midst and offers peace
Jesus appears only as a ghost
Jesus is invisible to the disciples
Jesus commands them to flee
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus stands in their midst and offers peace
questions.explanation: Luke 24:36 describes Jesus suddenly standing among the disciples and saying, 'Peace be unto you,' showing His real and peaceful presence after resurrection.

questions.question: How does Luke 24:27 demonstrate the importance of understanding Old Testament prophecy?
options: Jesus expounded all scriptures concerning Himself, showing fulfillment of prophecy
Prophecies were irrelevant after Jesus' death
Only New Testament is important for faith
Jesus ignored Old Testament teachings
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus expounded all scriptures concerning Himself, showing fulfillment of prophecy
questions.explanation: Luke 24:27 shows Jesus explaining to the disciples how Moses and the prophets spoke about Him, emphasizing the crucial role of prophecy in understanding Christ.

questions.question: What practical response did the disciples have after recognizing Jesus in Luke 24:33-35?
options: They immediately returned to Jerusalem to share the news
They hid in fear and silence
They disbelieved and dispersed
They sought to confront the authorities
questions.correctAnswer: They immediately returned to Jerusalem to share the news
questions.explanation: Luke 24:33-35 recounts that the disciples rose that same hour, returned to Jerusalem, and shared their experience and recognition of Jesus, showing prompt obedience and witness.

questions.question: According to Luke 24:20-21, what expectation did the disciples have about Jesus before His resurrection?
options: They trusted He would redeem Israel
They expected Him to be a political king immediately
They thought He would never be crucified
They doubted He was the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: They trusted He would redeem Israel
questions.explanation: Luke 24:20-21 shows the disciples expressing that they had hoped Jesus was the one to redeem Israel, revealing their messianic expectations.

questions.question: What lesson about hospitality can be drawn from Luke 24:29, where the disciples urge Jesus to stay with them?
options: Welcoming others can lead to spiritual blessing and revelation
Hospitality is unnecessary in faith
Only leaders deserve hospitality
Hospitality should be avoided to maintain purity
questions.correctAnswer: Welcoming others can lead to spiritual blessing and revelation
questions.explanation: In Luke 24:29, the disciples constrain Jesus to stay with them, and this act of hospitality leads to their eyes being opened, showing the value of welcoming others.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 24:31 states that the disciples recognized Jesus after He blessed and broke the bread.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 24:31 explicitly says 'their eyes were opened, and they knew him' after Jesus blessed and broke the bread.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 24:11, the disciples immediately believed the women's report about the empty tomb.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 24:11 states that 'their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not,' showing initial disbelief.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 24 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 24.

questions.question: In Luke 24:39, what proof does Jesus offer to show He is not a spirit?
options: Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.
I am the bread of life.
Touch my robe and feel the power within.
I am the Alpha and the Omega.
questions.correctAnswer: Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:39 clearly states Jesus invites them to handle His hands and feet as proof He is not a spirit.

questions.question: According to Luke 24:41-43, what did Jesus do when the disciples gave Him food?
options: He took it, and did eat before them.
He blessed it and distributed it to the crowd.
He refused to eat, saying He was still fasting.
He used it to teach a parable about provision.
questions.correctAnswer: He took it, and did eat before them.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:43 states Jesus took the food and ate it before the disciples to prove His physical resurrection.

questions.question: What does Jesus say in Luke 24:44 must be fulfilled?
options: All things which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.
The destruction of the temple.
The coming of Elijah before the Messiah.
The restoration of Israel as a political kingdom.
questions.correctAnswer: All things which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:44 explains Jesus referred to the fulfillment of scriptures about Him in the Law, Prophets, and Psalms.

questions.question: In Luke 24:45, what did Jesus do to the disciples' understanding?
options: Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.
He closed their ears so they would not hear false teachings.
He gave them a new language to communicate.
He told them to wait for the coming of the Spirit.
questions.correctAnswer: Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:45 states Jesus opened their understanding to comprehend the scriptures.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'promise of my Father' mentioned in Luke 24:49?
options: It refers to the coming of the Holy Spirit, empowering the apostles.
It is the promise of a political kingdom in Israel.
It is the promise of a new law to replace the Mosaic Law.
It signifies the rebuilding of the temple.
questions.correctAnswer: It refers to the coming of the Holy Spirit, empowering the apostles.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:49 shows Jesus telling them to wait in Jerusalem until they receive power from on high, referring to the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What action marks Jesus' departure in Luke 24:51?
options: He was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.
He ascended on a cloud and returned to the temple.
He disappeared in a pillar of fire.
He walked away into the wilderness.
questions.correctAnswer: He was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:51 describes Jesus being taken up into heaven in the presence of His disciples.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'epektasis' (ἐπέκτασις) in Luke 24:45 mean?
options: Extension or opening
Concealment
Confusion
Division
questions.correctAnswer: Extension or opening
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'epektasis' in Luke 24:45 refers to the 'opening' or 'extension' of understanding, as Jesus opened their minds to understand the scriptures.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Luke 24:37-43 where Jesus shows his hands and feet and eats before the disciples?
options: Inclusio
Chiasm
Metaphor
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Luke 24:37-43 uses inclusio by starting with the disciples’ fear and ending with Jesus eating to confirm His physical resurrection, framing the passage.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to Jesus’ statement in Luke 24:46 about Christ suffering and rising on the third day?
options: Jonah 1:17
Genesis 1:1
Exodus 20:12
Psalm 23:4
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah 1:17
questions.explanation: Luke 24:46’s reference to rising on the third day echoes Jonah 1:17 where Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and nights, a typology of resurrection.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of repentance and remission of sins preached to all nations as in Luke 24:47?
options: Acts 2:38
Romans 8:28
Revelation 21:4
Philippians 4:13
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 2:38
questions.explanation: Acts 2:38 echoes Luke 24:47’s theme where Peter calls to repent and be baptized for remission of sins, preached beginning at Jerusalem.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus opening the disciples' understanding in Luke 24:45?
options: Jesus explaining how all scriptures concerning Him must be fulfilled.
The disciples breaking bread with Jesus.
Jesus' ascension into heaven.
The women discovering the empty tomb.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus explaining how all scriptures concerning Him must be fulfilled.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:44 shows Jesus explaining the fulfillment of scriptures before verse 45 where He opens their understanding.

questions.question: What typological significance does Jesus eating broiled fish in Luke 24:42-43 carry in the Jewish cultural context?
options: It confirms His physical resurrection, countering the notion of a ghost or spirit.
It symbolizes the manna from heaven given to Israel.
It represents the Passover lamb sacrifice.
It indicates a new covenant meal replacing the old.
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms His physical resurrection, countering the notion of a ghost or spirit.
questions.explanation: In Luke 24:42-43, Jesus eating broiled fish demonstrates He has a physical body, important to Jewish understanding to counter spirit theories.

questions.question: How does the phrase 'Ye are witnesses of these things' in Luke 24:48 function within the narrative structure of the chapter?
options: It serves as a pivotal commissioning statement, marking the disciples as official witnesses and evangelists.
It is a rhetorical question emphasizing doubt.
It introduces a parable about witnessing.
It closes the chapter with a benediction.
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as a pivotal commissioning statement, marking the disciples as official witnesses and evangelists.
questions.explanation: Luke 24:48 functions as a commissioning statement emphasizing the disciples' role as witnesses of the resurrection and gospel.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 24:37, the disciples initially thought they had seen a spirit when Jesus appeared to them after His resurrection.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 24:37 states the disciples were terrified and supposed they had seen a spirit when Jesus appeared.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 24:53 reports that after Jesus’ ascension, the disciples stopped gathering in the temple.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 24:53 states the disciples were continually in the temple praising and blessing God, not that they stopped gathering.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 24 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 24 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 24:6 teach about salvation?
options: Christ's resurrection is essential for salvation
Salvation is by works and law keeping
Salvation is only for Israel
Salvation is through angelic intercession
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's resurrection is essential for salvation
questions.explanation: Luke 24:6 states 'He is not here, but is risen,' affirming the resurrection as a cornerstone of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning Christ's suffering does Luke 24:26 teach?
options: Christ's suffering was necessary to enter into His glory
Christ's suffering was accidental and avoidable
Christ did not need to suffer for humanity
Christ's suffering was only symbolic, not real
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's suffering was necessary to enter into His glory
questions.explanation: Luke 24:26 says, 'Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?' showing the necessity of His suffering.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of scripture in revelation does Luke 24:27 teach?
options: Jesus interprets the Old Testament as pointing to Himself
Scripture is unrelated to Jesus' mission
Only the New Testament reveals Christ
The Law is abolished with Christ's resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus interprets the Old Testament as pointing to Himself
questions.explanation: Luke 24:27 records Jesus expounding 'all the scriptures the things concerning himself,' showing scripture reveals Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 24:39 specifically demonstrate?
options: Omnipotence
Immutability
Incarnation
Eternity
questions.correctAnswer: Incarnation
questions.explanation: In Luke 24:39, Jesus emphasizes He has 'flesh and bones,' demonstrating the divine attribute of incarnation — God becoming man.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Luke 24:50 during Jesus' ascension?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Justice
Holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Luke 24:50 shows Jesus blessing and being 'carried up into heaven,' affirming His sovereign authority over all creation.

questions.question: How does Luke 24:44–47 connect this chapter to the broader theme of redemptive history in Scripture?
options: It shows Jesus fulfilling Old Testament prophecy concerning the Messiah
It rejects the Old Testament as irrelevant for Christians
It focuses exclusively on the New Testament
It denies the need for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Jesus fulfilling Old Testament prophecy concerning the Messiah
questions.explanation: Luke 24:44–47 speaks of fulfillment of 'law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms,' linking Jesus' work to redemptive history.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is emphasized by Luke 24:49 regarding the promise of the Father?
options: The coming of the Holy Spirit empowers the Church's mission
The promise refers only to earthly blessings
The promise is limited to the Jewish people
The promise replaces the covenant of grace
questions.correctAnswer: The coming of the Holy Spirit empowers the Church's mission
questions.explanation: Luke 24:49 promises the Father's gift of power from on high, referring to the Holy Spirit empowering believers for witness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 24:6 and Luke 24:46 teach about Christ's resurrection?
options: The resurrection is both a historical fact and a fulfillment of Scripture
The resurrection is a myth with no scriptural basis
The resurrection was only a spiritual event
The resurrection is independent from prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: The resurrection is both a historical fact and a fulfillment of Scripture
questions.explanation: Luke 24:6 declares 'He is risen,' a fact, while 24:46 shows it 'behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise,' fulfilling Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 24:25 and Luke 24:27 teach about the necessity of Christ's suffering?
options: Christ's suffering was foretold by the prophets and necessary for redemption
Christ's suffering was a surprise to the prophets
Suffering was irrelevant to Christ's mission
Prophetic writings deny Christ's suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's suffering was foretold by the prophets and necessary for redemption
questions.explanation: Luke 24:25 rebukes their slowness to believe the prophets, and 24:27 shows Jesus explaining scriptures concerning Himself, including suffering.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 24:39 and Luke 24:43 teach about Jesus' post-resurrection physicality?
options: Jesus' resurrection body was physical and capable of eating
Jesus' resurrection was purely spiritual without a body
Jesus appeared only as a ghost or vision
Jesus' body was transformed into an illusion
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' resurrection body was physical and capable of eating
questions.explanation: Luke 24:39 invites them to touch His flesh and bones; 24:43 records Him eating fish, confirming a physical resurrection body.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the resurrection appearances described in Luke 24 are hallucinations. What does Luke 24:36–43 actually teach?
options: Jesus' appearances were physical, evidenced by His eating and showing wounds
Jesus appeared only in visions without physical form
The disciples were deceived by spirits
The resurrection is symbolic, not literal
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' appearances were physical, evidenced by His eating and showing wounds
questions.explanation: Luke 24:39–43 shows Jesus inviting touch, showing wounds, and eating, demonstrating bodily resurrection appearances.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic witness does Luke 24:48 teach?
options: The apostles are witnesses to Christ's resurrection and teachings
Witnessing is optional for believers
The resurrection was not to be proclaimed publicly
Apostles rely on personal visions only
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles are witnesses to Christ's resurrection and teachings
questions.explanation: Luke 24:48 states, 'And ye are witnesses of these things,' underscoring apostolic testimony as foundation for the Church.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Luke 24:31 when the disciples recognize Jesus?
options: Omniscience
Revelatory grace
Wrath
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Revelatory grace
questions.explanation: Luke 24:31 shows Jesus opening their eyes to know Him, demonstrating God's gracious act of revelation to the disciples.

questions.question: What theological significance does the breaking of bread in Luke 24:30–31 convey?
options: It reveals Christ's presence and foreshadows the Lord’s Supper
It is merely a cultural meal with no spiritual meaning
It symbolizes parting and separation
It is an allegory for earthly food only
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals Christ's presence and foreshadows the Lord’s Supper
questions.explanation: Luke 24:30–31 describes Jesus blessing and breaking bread, which causes their eyes to open, prefiguring Eucharistic theology.

questions.question: How does Luke 24:53 contribute to the doctrine of sanctification in the early Church?
options: The disciples were continually praising God in the temple, showing growth in holiness
Sanctification was considered unnecessary after resurrection
The early Church abandoned temple worship
Sanctification was only individual and not communal
questions.correctAnswer: The disciples were continually praising God in the temple, showing growth in holiness
questions.explanation: Luke 24:53 describes the disciples 'continually in the temple, praising and blessing God,' indicating ongoing sanctification and worship.
